vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: black-fortress
Version: 1.1.4

The bundle is a security sandboxing framework that contains a critical shell injection vulnerability in `microvm_orchestrator.py` due to the use of `shell=True` with unsanitized directory paths in the Docker execution logic. While its stated purpose is defensive, it employs aggressive techniques such as automated code obfuscation (`deterministic_obfuscator.py`) and log sanitization (`fail_closed_postmortem.py`) to neutralize 'semantic' threats. It requires high-privilege access to Docker and kernel features (eBPF), which are high-risk capabilities, though they appear aligned with the tool's documented sandboxing and interrogation protocol.

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and requirements are consistent with a pre-installation sandboxing/orchestration tool; nothing requested is disproportionate to that purpose, but running it grants control over Docker (and optionally kernel-level tracing), which you should understand before executing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (pre-installation sandboxing, 5-layer verification) match the provided scripts and SKILL.md. Required binaries (docker, python3) and optional Firecracker/root for micro-VMs are reasonable for container/VM orchestration and eBPF tracing. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or network endpoints are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the orchestrator instruct you to build/run a local Docker runner and execute layered scripts (transcript extraction, obfuscation, container/VM execution, eBPF/syscall auditing, entropy checks, output filtering, postmortem). This is within the stated scope, but the orchestrator runs the docker CLI and may mount and manage containers; Docker daemon access is powerful (can lead to host access if volumes or sockets are mounted). The skill also documents eBPF/kernel tracing which requires elevated privileges on the host (or a configured host component). The orchestrator notes Docker mode often lacks eBPF traces and Firecracker needs root — this is explicit. Review microvm_orchestrator.py for exact mount/volume and socket usage before running in production.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external install-download step; the SKILL.md instructs building a local Docker image from the bundled Dockerfile. All code is bundled with the skill—no remote URLs, package registry installs, or extract-from-URL steps are present in the provided files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, secrets, or external credentials. It uses the host docker binary if present. The only privilege-like resource it requires is access to Docker (and optionally root/KVM for micro-VMs/eBPF), which the documentation explains. No unrelated env vars or keys are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always: false and user-invocable: true. The skill does not declare forced persistence or modify other skills. It runs as a one-off orchestrator; the only elevated interactions are standard Docker/VM orchestration and optional kernel tracing described in the docs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it runs a deterministic, multi-layer sandbox pipeline using Docker (or optionally Firecracker) and local Python scripts. Before running it: 1) Review microvm_orchestrator.py (and any docker run commands) to see which host paths, volumes, or sockets it mounts—Docker/daemon control is powerful and can expose the host if misused. 2) Be aware that Kernel-level tracing (eBPF) and Firecracker require elevated privileges (root/KVM) — only enable those if you trust the environment and need that level of ground-truth. 3) The obfuscator creates a sanitized copy and removes comments/logs; ensure you keep the original source for human review (the skill claims transcript extraction runs prior to obfuscation). 4) Because the skill manipulates containers and may hash/inspect many files, run it first in an isolated environment (CI sandbox or throwaway machine). 5) If you need deeper assurance, inspect the omitted scripts (microvm_orchestrator and any other truncated files) to confirm there are no hidden remote endpoints, mounts of sensitive host directories, or code that sends data off-host.
